behaviour: Adds the optional subscribe and isReady members to the public RouteResolutionApi interface.
rules: 1. Both members are optional (`?`) so every existing implementation and mock still type-checks.

2. `subscribe?(listener: () => void): () => void;` with TSDoc: registers a listener that is called each time the route information of the app changes, for example once the app has finished loading; returns a function that removes the listener; consumers fall back to resolving once when it is missing.

3. `isReady?(): boolean;` with TSDoc: returns false while the app is starting up and only some of its routes are known, and true once all routes are known; implementations that omit it are treated as always ready.
4. Do not change resolve, RouteFunc or routeResolutionApiRef, and do not edit report.api.md (it is regenerated with yarn build:api-reports).

behaviour: RouteResolutionApiProxy tracks whether it holds the full route information, implements subscribe and isReady, and notifies subscribers on every initialize; the phase tree marks the bootstrap initialization as not ready.
rules: 1. Add private fields `#ready = false;` and `readonly #listeners = new Set<() => void>();` after #routeObjects.

2. initialize gains a third parameter `options: { ready: boolean }`; after setting #delegate and #routeObjects it sets `this.#ready = options.ready`, then calls every listener in `Array.from(this.#listeners)` (a copy, so a listener that unsubscribes does not disturb the loop), then returns routeInfo as before.
3. Add `subscribe(listener: () => void): () => void` that adds the listener to #listeners and returns `() => { this.#listeners.delete(listener); }`.
4. Add `isReady(): boolean` returning #ready (false before the first initialize).

5. In instantiateAndInitializePhaseTree pass `{ ready: !options.stopAtAttachment }` as the third initialize argument, with a one-line comment that only the bootstrap phase stops at the session boundary, so its route info is partial.
6. resolve, getRouteObjects, the constructor and every other class and function in the file stay unchanged.

behaviour: useRouteRef re-resolves the route ref when the route resolution API reports a change, with one re-render per change.
rules: 1. Import `useEffect, useMemo, useState` from 'react'.
2. After useApi, compute `const ready = routeResolutionApi.isReady?.() ?? true;` and `const [routeInfoVersion, setRouteInfoVersion] = useState(0);`.

3. Add `useEffect(() => { ... }, [routeResolutionApi, ready]);` that returns undefined when `routeResolutionApi.subscribe` is missing; otherwise calls `routeResolutionApi.subscribe(() => setRouteInfoVersion(v => v + 1))` as a method call on the API object, then, if `(routeResolutionApi.isReady?.() ?? true) !== ready`, calls `setRouteInfoVersion(v => v + 1)` once to catch a change that happened between render and subscribe, and returns the unsubscribe function.

4. Keep the useMemo body as `routeResolutionApi.resolve(routeRef, { sourcePath: pathname })`; its dependency array becomes `[routeResolutionApi, routeRef, pathname, routeInfoVersion]` with `// eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` on the line directly above the array.
5. Return routeFunc; the exported signature and TSDoc stay unchanged. An API without subscribe and isReady behaves exactly as before.

behaviour: The core-plugin-api useRouteRef bridge re-resolves on route resolution changes and, while the app is not ready, returns a link to the current location instead of throwing for a required ref.

3. The newRouteFunc useMemo keeps its body (null without an API, try resolve, catch returns null) and its dependency array becomes `[routeResolutionApi, routeRef, pathname, routeInfoVersion]` with `// eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` on the line directly above the array, so the arrow function and the array are separate arguments on their own lines.

In the `newRouteFunc !== null` branch, when the result is falsy and the ref is not optional: if `!ready`, return `(() => pathname) as RouteFunc<Params>` with a comment that the app is still starting and its page routes are not known yet; otherwise throw `No path for ${routeRef}` exactly as today.
